title: Provider Concentration x Correlated Eval Blind Spots: Shared Failures Pass the Same Tests

original_idea.body:
# Provider Concentration x Correlated Eval Blind Spots: Shared Failures Pass the Same Tests

**Problem:** Failure mode A is systemic risk from provider concentration (many systems built on the same base model). Failure mode B is correlated benchmark blind spots (a shared eval misses a shared flaw). The compound effect: derivatives of one base model fail identically on the untested region, and because they all pass the same benchmark, the correlated systemic risk is invisible to evaluation.

**Direction:** Take one open base model and 3-4 of its fine-tuned derivatives. Probe a harmful-behavior region and measure correlation of failures across derivatives vs across unrelated models. Show that derivative failures are highly correlated and that a standard benchmark, passed by all, hides this correlated risk.

**Why it matters:** The EU AI Act and IAISR2026 flag concentration as systemic risk, but benchmarks score models independently. Demonstrating failure correlation among derivatives with simple statistics argues for benchmarks that report inter-model failure correlation, not just per-model pass rates. Fully open-model and counterfactual to labs.

**Relevant context:** Subfield: 'Design evaluations for systemic risks from AI concentration' (EU AI Act, International AI Safety Report 2026). Builds on open base + derivative models freely available on HuggingFace.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlated failures across derivatives of a concentrated base model is a recognized systemic-risk pathway (EU AI Act); argues for inter-model failure-correlation metrics.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Clear inherited methodology (probe derivatives, compute failure correlation); novice + mentor can execute on HuggingFace models with basic stats.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable (correlation of failures across 3-4 derivatives vs unrelated models), few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, weak lab incentive to expose concentration risk; independent third-party scrutiny adds value.

low_compute.reasoning: A few small open models, inference only on a single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Inter-model failure correlation across derivatives appears largely unstudied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No direct published work on correlated-failure benchmarking of base-model derivatives known.
